revisions.reason: Two defects in the v1 PU-Bench mappings surfaced while auditing the nnPU/Spambase/cc/c=0.1 anchor. (1) All 15 PU mappings carried the CIFAR-10 preprocessing difference, the five Spambase rows included, although both sides fit train-only statistics there and no such difference exists. (2) All 15 omitted the training-view difference.

15 PU mappings: added the training-view difference
revisions.evidence: Replaying PU-Bench's own selection protocol over the 200 recorded checkpoints of each of our 5 os/ts runs reproduced the anchor on the ts view (80.91 +- 1.26 vs 81.66 +- 2.73, |delta| 0.75, 2*SE 2.06) while the os view and the paper-body macro-F1 protocol both miss it by 7-8pp. That is what identified the training view as a protocol difference rather than an implementation defect.

revisions.reason: The IMDB preprocessing difference registered by revision 1 does not hold. Revision 1 correctly identified the CIFAR-10 preprocessing line as wrongly copied onto dataset rows that do not carry that difference, and replaced it on the IMDB rows with an IMDB-specific line -- but the replacement was never itself checked. Our IMDB features are L2 unit-norm, the same convention as PU-Bench's locked code, so the two sides do not differ in preprocessing.
changed: 5 IMDB PU mappings: dropped the IMDB preprocessing difference
revisions.evidence: Our shipped split manifests record preprocessing.effective_output_normalization = 'l2_unit_norm' with normalization_source = 'model_pipeline_module' (model sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2); measured on the shipped data/splits/imdb/split_0/train.npz the per-row L2 norm is min 0.99999988 / max 1.00000012 / mean 1.00000000. PU-Bench's locked code applies _l2_normalize to X_train and X_test (data/IMDB_PU.py:226-234, commit 2d95a19; contradiction pu_bench_imdb_embedding_normalization). Both sides unit-norm => no difference.
